referenceComponents.label: Bento
referenceComponents.note: Six tiles, irregular spans. The largest carries the lead idea; smaller ones extend it.
referenceComponents.about: Bento - six tiles, irregular spans. The largest tile carries the lead idea; the smaller ones extend it. Spans break the 3x2 default AI grids reach for. No icons, no emoji decoration - typography supplies the variety.

referenceComponents.label: Tier bento
referenceComponents.note: Lead tier spans 2×2; supporting tiers smaller. Visual hierarchy expresses the recommendation.
referenceComponents.about: Tiered bento - pricing tiers laid out as a bento grid: the lead tier spans two columns + two rows; supporting tiers are smaller. Breaks the 3-equal-cards default; the visual hierarchy expresses the recommended tier.

heroGuidance: Compose the hero to fit the FIRST VIEWPORT (~1280×800, min-height:100svh): nav, headline, supporting line, primary CTA and any hero visual must be COMPLETE above the fold. Size display type to 2-3 balanced lines within that height - an oversized wordmark or heading eating the viewport is the single most common failure. Modest top spacing, not a tall empty gap.
spacingGuidance: Below the fold, two separate systems. VERTICAL: 80-160px between sections (measured median for the biggest step: 96px); under ~64px two sections read as one crammed block. Pick ONE rhythm (e.g. clamp(72px, 10vw, 140px)) and use it at every seam. HORIZONTAL: a centered max-width column with symmetric padding-inline (24px minimum on mobile) so copy never touches the edge; full-bleed is for backgrounds. Declare them separately - a container's padding SHORTHAND (.wrap{padding:0 32px}) outranks section{padding:96px 0} on the same element and silently zeroes the rhythm, so give the container padding-inline only. Verify: a mid-page section's computed block padding must not be 0px.
htmlNote: Writing a standalone HTML file? Include <meta charset="utf-8">. These exemplars lean on typographic glyphs (middle dots, arrows, true quotes) and render as mojibake without it.
tip: referenceComponents are archetype notes; get_reference_jsx({type,id}) for one's source. Study the 3 inline exemplar thumbnails (the remaining 2 carry image URLs; fetch one only if the first 3 don't fit the brief) for palette, type and density - the first two carry a fold-by-fold autopsy, the rest a northstar plus get_screen. Then honour heroGuidance and spacingGuidance. Budget: this call plus one or two searches and get_screen on the 3-5 references you keep is a complete study.
